summary: Trung Huynh is a scholar in Buddhist studies who completed a PhD at the University of the West, where he studied under doctoral supervisor Darui Long (attested 2016).

Trungram Gyaltrul Rinpoche (born 1968) works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Karma Shri Nalanda Institute (~1981–1990) and under Khenchen Trinley Paljor, Thomas Burke, and Leonard W. J. van der Kuijp at Harvard University (~1997–2004, PhD).

Trungram Gyalwa Rinpoche (born 1968) specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Karma Shri Nalanda Institute, Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, and Harvard University (PhD, 2004), holding visiting appointments at the University of Michigan and McGill University (2016).

Tryambak Shankar Shejwalkar (1895–1963) was an Indian scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology. Educated at the University of Mumbai, he served on the faculty of Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute from circa 1939 to 1955.
Tré Khen Zur Lozang Wangchuk studied under the 13th Dalai Lama, the 14th Dalai Lama, and Trijang Rinpoche.

Trịnh Xuân Thuận (born 1948) is a scholar in philosophy. He studied at the California Institute of Technology (~1967–1970) and Princeton University (~1970–1974), later joining the University of Virginia circa 1979.

Tse-fu Kuan works in Buddhist studies. He earned his doctorate at the University of Oxford under Richard Gombrich (1999–2004), later holding a postdoctoral post at National Cheng Kung University and a position at Yuan Ze University (attested 2015).
Tsenshab Serkong Rinpoche (1914–1983) worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Educated at Ganden Monastery, where he earned a Geshe Lharampa degree, he held a post at Ganden Jangtse Monastery.

Tsering Dhundup Gonkatsang (1951–2018) worked in Tibetology and linguistics. He studied at Panjab University, Tibetan Children's Village, and the University of Glasgow (1987), later serving as headmaster at Tibetan Children's Village and Tibetan instructor at Oxford (2001).

Tsering Shakya (born 1959) is a scholar of Tibetology, history, and archaeology. Educated at SOAS (BA, MPhil, PhD 2004), he held research posts at SOAS, taught at Oxford, and became a Research Chair at UBC circa 2005.

Tsikey Chokling Rinpoche (1953–2020) was active in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. Educated at the Young Lamas Home School, he served as master of Vajrayana ceremonies at Ka-Nying Shedrub Ling Monastery (~1976–2020).

Tsoknyi Rinpoche (born 1966) is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies figure. He studied at Khampagar Monastery (~1979–1990) under teachers including Khamtrul Rinpoche Dongyud Nyima, Adeu Rinpoche, and Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, and held a post at Tergar Osel Ling Monastery.

Tsuguhito Takeuchi (1951–2021) was a Tibetologist and linguist. He studied at Kyoto University, the University of Pennsylvania, and Indiana University Bloomington (PhD 1994), and served as Professor of Linguistics at Kobe City University of Foreign Studies (~1998–2017).

Tsugunari Kubo (1936–2019) worked in Buddhist studies and Indology. Educated at the University of Tokyo and Rissho University (Doctor of Letters, 1985), he taught at Rissho University and served as president of Reiyukai and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.

Tsukasa Mizushima (born 1952) is a historian and Indologist. He earned his degrees, including a doctorate (1992), from the University of Tokyo, where he was later professor (1997–2018), after holding faculty positions at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies.

Tsultrim Allione (born 1947) works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She studied under traditional teachers including Chögyam Trungpa, Apho Rinpoche, and Rangjung Rigpe Dorje, and completed a master's degree at Antioch University (~1985–1987).

Tsultrim Gyatso works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He has served as abbot of Drepung Gomang Dratsang (attested 1987) and as a senior instructor at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies.

Tsultrim Kelsang works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He held posts at the International Buddhist Association (attested 1973), Otani University as lecturer (attested 1984) and professor (attested 1999–2002), and Ryukoku University as an open-recruitment researcher (2015).

Tsuneki Nishiwaki (born 1943) is a scholar in Sinology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. Educated at Tokyo University of Education (~1963–1972), he served as a professor at Kyoto University (~1990–2007) and held a post at Doshisha University (~2007–2014).

Tsung-i Jao (1917–2018) was a scholar in Sinology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. Educated at Shantou Jinshan Middle School, he held academic posts at the University of Hong Kong, the National University of Singapore, Yale University, and the EPHE.
